What factors might be driving trends in solving the Millennium Prize problems?
There are three main classes of solution-near foreclosure:

  - Loss of enthusiasm, interest, or funding for early-stage research.
  - Recognition that important areas for problem tackling are fully subsumed by existing solutions.

## Yang-Mills existence and mass gap

A mathematical structure is strongly solved if (1) it exists in the abstract; (2) its functional and algebraic properties are well-understood; (3) it generates useful solutions to a wide range of problems in applied mathematics if used properly; and (4) there is a computationally feasible algorithm for transporting from its abstract form to useful applied form.

Progress has been made on ensuring the naïve definition of Yang-Mills theory, or even simpler variants of that theory, meets these criteria. Most of this progress has been focused on aspects of it that are widely thought to be instrumental in undermining its ability to properly form and obtain rigorous minimal constants that characterize the fundamental interactions of the Standard Model. Simulation-based mass gap limits based on analytic Yang-Mills theory have at least previously sustained mathematical investigation.

## Hodge conjecture

For some classes of vectors that appear naturally in engineering and physics, there are computational algorithms that use a polynomial number of terms to exactly mimic and replace infinite sequences of polynomials. Usually, these algorithms make great reductions in computation complexity if they can avoid attention to the original vector problem for the polynomial series. The Hodge conjecture weak (likely exponential-complexity) matrix-inversion refutation to these polynomial-based algorithms is unknown. It is indirectly related to the Smale 17th Hilbert Problem via diagonalization structures in matrix forms. Furthermore, computing the Hodge conjecture exactly for matrices means solving the World's Hardest Linear Algebra Problem. The Hodge conjecture is closely related to the open non-polynomial complexity issues characterized by lower-bounding the computational complexity of the permanent. Even proving the Hodge conjecture no-constant determination of the permanent, or the permanent-parity test of a matrix, or the permanent non-sign condition of the permanent on matrices, seems daunting.

Perhaps the ... single most interesting explicit conditional separation of purely exponential algorithms ("P") from linear but non-constant algorithms ("NP; e.g., polynomial). Jared put it "purists may complain about imperialist outreach, but this whole purist obsession with exponentials is pretty absurd. In practice, people routinely speed up purely exponential routines into ppoly(log n) time. Fundamental to us understanding the true behavior and importance of exponential systems, as well as tuned tools to deal with them, is a way to prove powerful lower bounds in the world of pure exponentials can be solved with low communication complexity".
